title: C1539 — Ignition coil-on-plug 2
introduction:
The ignition coil makes the high voltage needed at the spark plug. This reference explains its connector’s wiring identities, and I read it like an address book: find the cavity in the picture, then let the matching row introduce the circuit and its job. The plastic outline gets you oriented on the page; the labels do the real navigating.

Begin with the connector identity, read the cavity-to-circuit map, then consult the separate pigtail listing for service-part identification. A similar-looking housing alone does not establish vehicle or engine applicability. This is a reading guide, not an access, probing, diagnostic or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are unspecified here; keep those entries as printed without inventing their interpretation.

edits.why: The cavity labels sit vertically within the drawing’s tall oval area. I use the broad rectangular feature on the left and the projection on the right as landmarks within this illustration. The nearby shell-and-harness identification table ties the picture to its reference entry.

Match an illustrated cavity label to the Cavity column, then read across its row for circuit identity, color code, listed gauge, function and terminal part. The function descriptions distinguish powertrain control, chassis/battery ground and power supply. Those descriptions explain the assigned connections; they do not prove electrical continuity, coil operation or the cause of a misfire.

I read the kit Number alongside Service Part and Engineering Shell to keep the pigtail’s catalog identity associated with its housing. The other columns record the listed pigtail attributes and catalog-image filename. Keep that assembly entry distinct from the terminal entry in the pin table; finding a terminal identifier is not the same as identifying the complete pigtail.
